editorial:
Rusty Griswold is all grown up now, and he wants to give his own kids the same magical road trip he had as a kid. So he packs up his wife and two sons and heads across the country to Walley World, the coolest theme park around. But as you can guess, nothing goes according to plan. The family runs into one disaster after another, from gross hotel rooms to awkward encounters with relatives. The whole movie has that classic road trip energy where every stop brings a new problem, and you can't help but laugh at how badly things keep going wrong.

The cast really sells the chaos. Ed Helms plays Rusty with just the right mix of optimism and panic, and Christina Applegate keeps things grounded as his wife. The kids are funny too, especially the younger son who has a wild streak. Some jokes land harder than others, and a few scenes push the gross-out humor a bit too far. Still, if you enjoy silly, over-the-top comedy with a heart, this is a fun ride. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the Griswolds finally reach Walley World, but the park is closed for repairs. Rusty refuses to give up and sneaks the family inside anyway. They end up riding the roller coaster just as security catches up. Instead of getting arrested, the family bonds over the wild ride and realizes the trip was never about the destination. The movie ends with them driving home, closer than before, with a new appreciation for their messy family.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves silly road trip comedies with heart
